Gāthāsaptaśatī,
skt>gAthAkoza, prAkRtasaptazatI, zRGgArasaptazatI, saptazatI, or sattasaI anthology of sevenhundred Pkt. gāthās by Hāla Śātavāhana or Śālivāhana; for a discussion on its original name, see V. V. Mirashi, XIIIth AIOC. Nagpur 1946. Only 430 verses are common to all the six extant recensions; assigned to different dates by scholars: 1st Cent. B. C., K. G. Sankar, ABORI. XII. p.. 311-2; 1st or 2nd Cent. A. D. (Wint. HIL. III. (Eng. transl.). Pt. i. p. 115); from 200-450 A. D. (Keith, His.. of Skt. Lit. p. 224); 3rd Cent. A. D. (Weber); 4th Cent. A. D. V. V. Mirashi, IHQ. XXIII. p.. 300-310, on the basis of the dates of some later royal authors whose names are found in the collection; 6th Cent. A. D. D. R. Bhandarkar, Commemora- [Page342-b] tive Essays presented to R. G. Bhandarkar, p. 189. See also M. L. Mathur, Nāgarī Pracāriṇī Pattrikā 56. p.. 252-85. Ref. to by Bāṇa, Harṣacarita, Intro. verse 13; according to Abhinanda (Rāmacarita, GOS. edn. XLVI. p. 296) the real author seems to be Śrīpālita. (hAlenottamapUjayA kavivRSA zrIpAlito lAlitaH). On Sātavāhana a. a Kuntala king an. Prākṛt enthusiast see also Kāvyamīmāṁsā, GOS. edn. of 1934, p.. 50. 55; explanatory notes p.. 197. 203-5; also A. N.
